source_evidence.observation: The input format has precision t, unit roundoff u, and maximum normalized value fmax; the accumulation format has precision T >= t, unit roundoff U, and maximum normalized value Fmax. Assuming no overflow, input conversion satisfies fl(z) = z(1 + delta) + eta with |delta| <= u, |eta| <= gmin, and eta delta = 0.

source_evidence.anchor: prose following equation (2.3), equation (2.4), and rounding-mode paragraph
source_evidence.observation: The operator fl rounds a real value to the nearest number representable in the input format. The stated models assume round-to-nearest; directed rounding is covered only after doubling the corresponding roundoff and underflow constants.

source_evidence.anchor: section 3 opening, equation (3.1), and following scaling assumptions
source_evidence.observation: For A in R^(m x n) and B in R^(n x q), the scaling scheme is C = Lambda^(-1)(fl(Lambda A) fl(BM))M^(-1), where Lambda and M are nonsingular diagonal matrices. Their diagonal scaling factors are assumed to be powers of two to avoid scaling-roundoff errors.

source_evidence.anchor: continuation of the assumptions following equation (3.1)
source_evidence.observation: Underflow and overflow are assumed absent before the Lambda and M scaling and after the inverse scaling; equivalently, A, B, and C are stored in a sufficiently high precision format to be represented exactly.

Theta is the maximum value allowed in the exact scaled matrices Lambda A and BM. The maximum coefficient magnitude on every scaled row and column is intended to lie in (theta/2, theta]. Input overflow requires theta <= fmax, accumulation overflow requires theta <= sqrt(Fmax/n), and the paper prescribes theta = min(fmax, sqrt(Fmax/n)).
For an inner product x^T y with x a row of A, its row scaling factor lambda is a power of two satisfying theta/(2||x||_infinity) < lambda <= theta/||x||_infinity.

The later conversion fl(lambda x) may still incur either ordinary input-format rounding or input underflow componentwise. Thus the exactness attributed to power-of-two scaling does not make the subsequent conversion fl exact.
